newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea wants dlr to move below 895 won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea wants dlr to move below 895 won.

text.p: The South Korean central bank wants the dollar to weaken against the local currency and firmly intends to stabilise the won/dollar rate, a Bank of Korea official said on Monday.
"We want the dollar to move below the 895 won level," the official said. "Without changes in economic fundamentals, there is no doubt the dollar would weaken (versus the local currency)."
He said the central bank, concerned about the economy, would "aggressively react" to any speculative dollar buying.
A financial crisis at the nation's eighth largest conglomerate, Kia Group, battered the local currency last week. Creditor banks decided to bail out Kia Group last week.
The dollar stood at 895.00 won at 0120 GMT after opening at 894.70. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
